Research Assistant / Associate in power electronics
Requisition ID:  29975
Location:  

Newcastle, GB

Contract Type:  Fixed Term
Working Pattern:  Full Time
Posted Date:  27 Nov 2026

Salary:

Research Assistant: £34,630 to £36,320 per annum

Research Associate: £37,369 to £45,641 per annum

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 11 December 2026

 

The Role

 

We are excited to offer an opportunity for a Research Assistant/Associate in power electronics to join the School of Engineering at Newcastle University and contribute to research on the next generation of intelligent and resilient electricity distribution networks. 

 

You will join Newcastle University's Electrical Power research group, working within a collaborative team with expertise spanning power electronics, electrical power systems and electrical machines technologies. The post is based at Newcastle University and will involve interaction with academic and industrial collaborators, including colleagues at the University of Edinburgh. 

 

The research is part of an EPSRC-funded collaborative project between Newcastle University and the University of Edinburgh, which aims to advance hybrid distribution transformers by integrating power-electronic functionality with distribution transformer technology, enabling enhanced control and support for future electricity networks. Recent project research has developed and investigated a modified hybrid distribution transformer with magnetically integrated power-electronic modules. The next stage will build on this work and explore how the platform can support advanced grid-forming functions and other grid-supporting functions. 

 

The candidate will join an EPSRC-funded collaborative research project between Newcastle University and the University of Edinburgh focused on developing next-generation hybrid distribution transformers through the integration of power-electronic modules and advanced control. Building on research into a modified transformer with magnetically integrated power-electronic modules, the project will continue the development, modelling, optimisation and validation of the hybrid transformer architecture and advance its potential to provide grid-forming functionality and support resilient electricity distribution networks. The candidate will contribute to research delivery, work collaboratively with the project team and partners, and help generate high-quality research outputs.

 

As the successful candidate, you will contribute to the modelling, design, optimisation, control and experimental validation of the hybrid transformer and its integrated power-electronic modules. You will also help advance grid-forming control and investigate its application within the wider distribution network context. The role offers the opportunity to contribute to ongoing research while helping shape the next phase of the project. 

 

We are particularly interested in candidates with a strong background in power electronics, including converter modelling and control, and experience in simulation and/or experimental investigation. Knowledge of power transformers, magnetic components, grid-connected converters or grid-forming control would be valuable. We welcome applicants who work collaboratively, communicate findings clearly and contribute to high-quality research outputs. 

 

The post is full-time (37 hours per week) and fixed term until July 2027 and will be based at Newcastle University.  

 

We follow the Researcher Development Concordat: Researcher Development | Our Research | Newcastle University. We enable all colleagues to fulfil their research potential regardless of career stage. This commitment secures our thriving research culture and vibrant research environment. Our offer to each individual and their researcher development includes mentoring, annual research planning discussions, pooled research funding to support career development and research activities, peer review support for the development of research and innovation funding applications’. 

 

We want you to feel confident when applying for a position with Newcastle University. If you’d like an informal discussion to clarify any points, please contact Dr Mohamed Dahidah at mohamed.dahidah@ncl.ac.uk . We are committed to making the process accessible to everyone and can provide additional support to adjustments to meet your needs’ 

  

To apply, please complete an online application and upload a CV and cover letter explaining how your qualifications, experience and skills meet the essential criteria. Please include examples of relevant work in power-electronics modelling/control, transformer or magnetic-component research, and simulation or experimental validation.

 

As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf.  These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level. 

 

Find out more about the Faculty of Science, Agriculture and Engineering (SAgE) here: Faculty of Science, Agriculture & Engineering | Faculty of Science, Agriculture & Engineering | Newcastle University 

 

Contact for the post is mohamed.dahidah@newcastle.ac.uk

 

Duration of post is until 08 July 2027 

 

Key Accountabilitites

Research Assistant

Collect, analyse and interpret research data and draw conclusions on the outcomes
Co-ordinate own work with that of others, use problem solving to affect the achievement of research objectives and contribute to the planning of the project(s)
Present information on research progress and outcomes to a Principal Investigator or groups overseeing the research project
Write up results from own research activity and provide input into the research project’s dissemination, in whatever form (report, papers, chapters, books)
Use research resources (including, where required, laboratories, workshops and specialist equipment) as appropriate
Undertake modelling, simulation, design and experimental investigation of hybrid distribution transformers incorporating magnetically integrated power-electronic modules
Contribute to the electromagnetic design, optimisation and characterisation of transformer structures, including analysis of magnetic coupling, flux distribution and transformer performance
Develop, implement and validate control strategies for integrated power-electronic converters, including grid-forming control techniques and their application to future distribution networks
Operate, commission and experimentally evaluate the existing hybrid transformer and integrated power-electronic prototype, undertaking laboratory testing, performance characterisation and validation of its operation, and implementing modifications or improvements as required to support the progression of the research
Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, high-quality journal and conference publications, and dissemination of research findings to academic and industrial collaborators

Research Associate

Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project
Determine appropriate methodologies for research
Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations
Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination, either through seminar and conference presentations or through publications
Present research findings, either at conferences or through publications in reputable outlets appropriate to the discipline
Contribute to grant applications submitted by others and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding

 

The Person

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

Research Assistant

Attention to detail and ability to work at high levels of accuracy
Ability to present complex information effectively to a range of audiences
Proven ability to analyse data and write-up results
Experience of working collaboratively with colleagues
Excellent IT skills in all major office applications
The ability to use personal initiative and creativity to solve research problems
Strong knowledge of power electronic converters, including their modelling, simulation, design and control
Experience in modelling and simulation of power electronic systems using MATLAB/Simulink and/or other relevant simulation platforms
Knowledge of power transformers and magnetic components, including transformer modelling, magnetic circuit principles and electromagnetic performance
Experience in developing or implementing control strategies for power electronic converters, with an understanding of grid-connected converter operation and grid-forming control concepts
Experience in experimental investigation of power electronic systems, including laboratory testing, measurement, commissioning and validation of simulation results

In addition for Research Associate

Awareness of the research environment
High level of analytical and problem solving capacity
Ability to communicate complex information with clarity
Experience of presentations at conferences and/or in high quality publications

 

Attributes and Behaviour

Commitment to working positively as a member of a multi-skilled research team
Ability to negotiate and prioritise multiple, competing responsibilities and to work to deadlines
Commitment to continued professional development
An ability to work inclusively and respectfully with individuals from a wide range of backgrounds, recognising the value that diverse perspectives bring to an academic community and balancing the rights of academic freedom and freedom of speech within the law. 

 

Qualifications

Research Assistant

Honours degree in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Power Engineering or a closely related discipline

In addition for Research Associate

PhD in Power Electronics, Electrical Power Engineering, Power Systems or a closely related discipline

 

 

Newcastle University is a global University where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.  As a University of Sanctuary, we aim to provide a welcoming place of safety for all, offering opportunities to people fleeing violence and persecution.

 

We are committed to being a fully inclusive university which actively recruits, supports and retains colleagues from all sectors of society.  We value diversity as well as celebrate, support and thrive on the contributions of all of our employees and the communities they represent.  We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams, we believe that success is built on having teams whose backgrounds and experiences reflect the diversity of our university and student population.

 

At Newcastle University we hold a Gold Athena Swan award in recognition of our good employment practices for the advancement of gender equality.  We also hold a Race Equality Charter Bronze award in recognition of our work towards tackling race inequality in higher education REC.  We are a Disability Confident employer and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for the role as part of the offer and interview scheme.

 

In addition, we are a member of the Euraxess initiative supporting researchers in Europe.

Research Associate in Probability/Combinatorics

Job id: 164785. Salary: £46,004 - £48,399 per annum including London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 26 November 2026. Closing date: 10 December 2026.

Business unit: Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sci. Department: Mathematics.

Contact details: Dr Matthew Jenssen. matthew.jenssen@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Strand Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us 

King’s College London is one of the UK’s leading research universities, located in the heart of London. The Department of Mathematics is part of the Faculty of Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sciences and is based at the Strand Campus.

The post holder will join the Probability group, which offers an active research environment with a weekly seminar and regular reading groups. The group’s research spans discrete and continuous probability, with strong links to combinatorics, statistical physics and theoretical computer science.

About the role 

We invite applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Probability/Combinatorics to work with Dr Matthew Jenssen in the Department of Mathematics at King’s College London. The position is supported by a UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship, and there is flexibility in the start date.

The successful candidate will conduct research as part of the UKRI-funded project “Advancing Statistical Physics Methods in Combinatorics, Algorithms, and Geometry”. They will carry out individual and collaborative research, write up their results for publication, present their work at conferences and contribute ideas for new research projects. They will also contribute to the activities of the Probability group, for instance by participating in internal seminar series and reading groups. 

The role offers the opportunity to establish a strong track record of high-quality publications, to deepen our collective understanding of the subject, and to share that understanding widely through talks, seminars and collaboration. The post holder will be expected to keep up to date with advances in the field and translate them into new research, to help foster inter-disciplinary working within the department, and to take on departmental roles as may reasonably be required, such as helping to co-ordinate a seminar programme.

The post holder will report to Dr Matthew Jenssen (Principal Investigator).

This is a full time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 24 months.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: 

Essential criteria 

PhD awarded in Mathematics or a related discipline* 
Sufficient specialist knowledge in one or more of the following fields: Probability, Combinatorics, and Algorithms 
Ability to work within established research programmes related to the fields above 
Ability to manage own academic research and associated activities 
Previous experience of contributing to publications/presentations 
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to write for publication, present research proposals and results, and represent the research group at meetings 

Desirable criteria

An underlying vision which motivates their research 
Good organisational skills (e.g. experience in organising scientific events) 

Downloading a copy of our Job Description 

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6. 

Further information

At King’s, we believe that the diversity of our community and a culture that is welcoming, open, inclusive and collaborative, are great strengths of the university. 

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. At times, this will include balancing rights and beliefs that can feel in tension.

We are committed to free speech and to academic freedom, believing that our foundational purpose as a university, is to create spaces where a wide range of ideas, including ideas that are controversial, can be discussed and debated, and where members of our community can express lawful views without fear of intimidation, harassment or discrimination.

When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving rapidly, and we recognise its growing role in professional work. Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews or assessment activities unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found here.

We reserve the right to close adverts early due to the volume of applications we receive. While the closing date may change, all adverts will close at 23:59 to allow sufficient time for applications to be submitted on that day.

We encourage you to apply at the earliest opportunity to avoid disappointment as once we have closed a vacancy you will be unable to submit your application.

To find out how our managers will review your application, please take a look at our ‘How we Recruit’ pages.

Interviews are due to be held on the week of 18/01/2027.

The Role

The National Waste and Recycling Robotics Adoption Hub (NORAH) is looking for a Robotics and AI Researcher to help UK waste and recycling businesses adopt robotics, automation and artificial intelligence.

You will join the NORAH team at Kingston University and work directly with industry partners, technology providers and end users. You will develop, adapt and test AI and computer vision solutions for real-world recycling challenges, such as detecting, identifying and sorting materials, and you will help turn research into technology that businesses can use.

Your main responsibilities will include designing and evaluating computer vision and machine learning models for robotic sorting and inspection, running trials and demonstrations with industry partners, assessing which technologies best suit an end user's needs, and sharing results through technical reports, publications, workshops and events. You will also contribute to the Hub's engagement with businesses, translating technical capabilities into clear benefits for companies considering robotics and AI.

The Person

You will have a strong background in artificial intelligence and computer vision, ideally demonstrated through a PhD in a relevant field such as computer science, AI, robotics or engineering. We will also consider candidates with a Master's degree who can show a strong and relevant research or industry track record. You will be confident developing and evaluating deep learning models for vision tasks and taking ideas from prototype to working system.

Experience in robotics would be a significant advantage, as would knowledge of recent developments such as agentic AI, large foundation models and vision-language-action models. Just as important, you will be a clear communicator who can explain technical work to non-specialist audiences, with an interest in, or knowledge of, business-to-business engagement and how companies adopt new technology.

The Faculty

NORAH, the National Waste and Recycling Robotics Adoption Hub, is funded by Innovate UK and led by Kingston University. The Hub brings together universities, technology providers and industry partners to help businesses in the UK waste and recycling sector understand, trial and adopt robotics, automation and AI, improving productivity, safety and recycling performance.

The Hub sits within Kingston University's Faculty of Engineering, Computing and the Environment, where research in AI, computer vision and robotics is applied to real industrial challenges, including waste and textile recycling. Joining NORAH means working in a collaborative team with direct links to industry, contributing to a national programme that supports the UK's move towards a circular economy.

Further information

This is a full-time, fixed-term position for 12 months with a starting salary of £34,687 per annum.

Interviews are expected to take place on 15 January 2027.

For informal enquiries, please contact Professor Vasileios Argyriou, NORAH Director.

Bring your true self, expertise, and passion to Kingston where we are continuing to strive to build a university where authentic inclusion and belonging is at its heart. Every one of our staff and students’ identities, backgrounds and diverse experiences makes us who we are - so harness and embrace yours by applying today. We welcome applications from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic backgrounds, LGBTQ+ communities and those with disabilities.

We are a place-based organisation, proud of our location in Kingston and the civic role we play in our community. Our campuses inspire collaborative, innovative and creative communities. Being present on campus is important to us because it helps us to create a sense of belonging for both our staff and students. Therefore, staff are expected to be on campus for the majority of their working week.

Candidates must be able to demonstrate their eligibility to work in the UK in accordance with the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006. Where required, this may include entry clearance or continued leave to remain under the Points Based Immigration Scheme. 

To apply click on ‘Apply Now’. If, for accessibility reasons, you need to apply in an alternative format, please email jobs@kingston.ac.uk or call the HR Shared Services team on 020 8417 3118.

Job Title: Research Fellow

Reference:  650             

Department: Physics

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 31 January 2030

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Sunday 3 January 2027, 11:59pm (UK)                       

Full time Salary Range: £37,369 - £46,970 per annum

About the Role

This is an exciting opportunity to join the  A. D. Wright Lab within the Department of Physics at the University of Warwick.

 

We are seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Assistant to undertake experimental research on spectroscopy of gas-phase polaritons, as part of an ERC-funded project. The successful candidate will help build the polariton spectroscopy setup. Subsequently they will establish, and employ, a methodology for studying chemical dynamics in the gas phase under vibrational strong coupling.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are looking for someone with a PhD in Physics, Physical Chemistry, or a related subject, with experience of spectroscopy using a free-space optical setup. Experience of optical cavity fabrication, cryogenics and/or gas-phase spectroscopy would also be appealing in a candidate.

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5. Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6.

About the Department

The A. D. Wright Lab uses spectroscopic techniques to probe the quantum-scale properties of complex systems. The group’s research interests lie in the optoelectronic properties of physically intriguing novel materials and systems, involving topics such as photophysical and nano-scale effects, charge-carrier dynamics, polaritonic effects and light harvesting for solar energy conversion. The A. D. Wright Lab is part of Warwick Quantum, and the wider Ultrafast & THz Photonics Group.

 

Department of Physics

The post will be based in the Department of Physics, a vibrant academic department with over 200 academic, research, technical and professional services staff, over 800 undergraduate students and 200 postgraduate research students.

We are proud of our diverse community of staff, students, and visitors, and are committed to maintaining excellence in both teaching and research by promoting equality of opportunity for all, within a culture of mutual respect and dignity.

We are pleased to hold an Institute of Physics Inclusion Award in support of our commitment to creating a welcoming and inclusive environment. 

Further information about working in the Department of Physics and the benefits available can be found at www.warwick.ac.uk/physics/staff/working/.

 The University supports flexible working and requests for part-time working or job-share will be considered where possible.

 

Childcare for interviews

Childcare can be provided for you at the University of Warwick Nursery (www.warwick.ac.uk/services/childrensservices/nursery) in order for you to attend the interview. Childcare is subject to availability of places at the Nursery.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated. 

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed in January 2027.

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.

 

Right to Work

 

If you do not yet have the right to work in the UK and/or are seeking sponsorship for a Skilled Worker visa, please follow this link which contains further information about obtaining the right to work in the UK.

Job Title: Research Fellow

Contract Type: Fixed-Term Contract
Contract End Date: 1 October 2027
Hours: Part-Time (0.4 FTE)
Full-Time Salary Range: £37,369 to £46,970 per annum (pro rata if part-time)

 

About the Role

 

We are seeking a part-time Research Fellow (0.4 FTE) to join an exciting Education Endowment Foundation (EEF)-funded evaluation of the Regional Partnerships programme. Led by Dr Tom Perry, this major research project explores how evidence-informed practice can support school improvement across England through collaboration between schools, trusts, Research Schools and local authorities. 

 

Working as part of an established research team, you will take a leading role in fieldwork and preliminary analysis across a mixed-methods evaluation involving eight Regional Partnerships. You will conduct interviews and focus groups, engage with school and trust leaders, manage and prepare research data, contribute to analysis and reporting, and help generate insights that inform educational policy and practice.

 

This is primarily a remote role, offering flexibility and the opportunity to work with colleagues from both the University of Warwick and Manchester Metropolitan University. Regular travel to schools, trusts and partnership events across the North of England will be required, with travel and subsistence costs covered.

 

About You

 

You will be an organised and motivated researcher with experience of conducting research in educational settings and a strong understanding of the English school system. You will either hold a doctorate in education or a related discipline, or be close to completing one, and have experience of qualitative or mixed-methods research, including data collection, preparation and analysis.

 

You will be confident engaging professionally with a wide range of stakeholders, including school leaders, teachers and partnership organisations, and possess excellent communication and organisational skills. You should be comfortable working independently as part of a geographically distributed team, managing multiple priorities and maintaining accurate records. 

 

We would particularly welcome applications from candidates with interests in professional learning and development, evidence use in education, school improvement, partnership working, educational disadvantage or realist evaluation approaches. Experience with tools such as NVivo and familiarity with EEF-funded research projects would be advantageous. 

 

Whether you are an early-career researcher looking to develop your expertise or an experienced education researcher seeking a flexible, impactful project, this role offers an opportunity to contribute to nationally significant research that aims to improve outcomes for pupils across England.

 

About the Department

 

The School of Education, Learning and Communication Sciences comprises of Applied Linguistics, Education Studies, Centre for Lifelong Learning and the Centre for Teacher Education.

 

With over 200 staff and 1800 students, including 150 doctoral students, we work with many partners including professional bodies and over 500 schools. SELCS is a welcoming and inclusive community, fostering excellence in research, impact, teaching and regional engagement across all its areas of expertise.

 

Research is central to the School’s new strategy, and we are dedicated to fostering an environment that promotes collaboration, innovation, and impact. As part of SELCS, you will play a key role in supporting this exciting growth and contributing to the School's continued success.

 

For further information about SELCS and the Centre for Education Studies please visit our website: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/selcs/

 

How to Apply

 

To apply, please click APPLY below and submit an application form by the closing deadline.

 

You will be asked to add your personal details and include two attachments:

 

CV
Cover Letter

 

These attachments should:

 

Outline employment and education history (including your most recent employment).
Demonstrate your skills, experience, and qualifications, and how you meet the essential and desirable criteria in the Job Description (attached below).

 

Please ensure your application clearly evidences the essential criteria, as the hiring panel may not be able to shortlist your application if these are not demonstrated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage candidates to submit an application as early as possible.

 

Interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed.

 

Job Description

 

For more information about essential and desirable knowledge, skills, experience, and qualifications for this position, please refer to the Job Description (JD) by clicking the link below:

 

↪ JD - Research Fellow (653)

 

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5.

 

Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow level, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6.

At the University of Warwick, you will have access to a wide range of benefits.

 

an attractive pension scheme;
a leading annual leave allowance;
excellent learning and development opportunities;
savings and discounts on a wide range of products and services;
generous maternity, paternity, and adoption leave;
onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work-life balance and support flexible working where this is compatible with the requirements of the role. Click here to find out more.

 

We are proud to be a Living Wage Employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, our Relocation Guide provides information about working at the University of Warwick and what may be involved in the relocation process.

 

Culture

 

At the University of Warwick, committed to creating a community built on mutual respect and dignity, and a welcoming working and learning environment.

 

We recognise and value the visible and non-visible differences within our community. Wherever possible, we seek to go beyond our legal obligations by removing economic, social, and cultural barriers to creating an environment in which everyone has the opportunity to thrive and achieve their full potential.

postings.listing_context: Research Fellowship Sponsorship Scheme Department of Genetics Research 27 November 2026 11 February 2027 PC44210
postings.advert_text:
The Department of Genetics at the University of Cambridge invites expressions of interest from early career researchers who wish to be sponsored for external fellowships to establish an independent research group.

Successful candidates will be of the highest calibre, with an exceptional track record for their career stage and the potential to submit competitive fellowship applications. The department will assist with the development of your fellowship application and practice for interviews. If successful, we have a programme of support to establish your independence as an academic researcher, including setting up your lab and recruiting personnel, as well as mentoring and training to help you develop your career. You will also be supported by the Cambridge Biological Sciences Research Fellowships Framework (www.bio.cam.ac.uk/research/research-fellowships) and peer-to-peer mentoring through the early PI network (www.bio.cam.ac.uk/biological-sciences-early-pi-network). You will have group leader status equivalent to tenured staff, playing a full role in running the department and will be given opportunities to gain experience in undergraduate and postgraduate teaching.

The Department of Genetics provides a world class, highly interactive and supportive research environment within the School of Biological Sciences at Cambridge. Research Themes (www.bio.cam.ac.uk/research/research-themes) span the School, providing opportunities to network across disciplines and Departments. The department is diverse, covering a wide range of topics in fundamental genetics and the application of genetic approaches across the biological and biomedical sciences. We are interested in candidates across this range whose research would benefit from and enhance our research environment. Target fellowships include NERC Independent Fellowship, ERC Starting and Consolidator Grants, Wellcome Trust Career Development Award, Royal Society University Research Fellowship, Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship, Branco-Weiss Research Fellowship, MRC Career Development Awards and BBSRC David Phillips Fellowship.

We will support our fellows to develop into strong candidates for Principal Investigator positions in the department or elsewhere. In line with this ethos, we have an excellent record of our past departmental fellows progressing to permanent positions in the University and other institutions.

As a department we are committed to a working culture that celebrates and promotes equality, diversity, and inclusion. We therefore encourage expressions of interest from women, people with disabilities, and people from Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds, as they are underrepresented at senior levels in our university. The opportunity is open to candidates from within the UK and internationally.

Further Details

The Department runs an open and competitive selection process to select the best candidates it will sponsor for fellowship applications. The deadline for applications is rolling, however please keep in mind the time needed to review your application ahead of each fellowship deadline. To initiate this, please send a CV, a 1-page outline of your future research plans, the names of two referees and a cover letter explaining why you are a good fit for the Department, to Sam Laister HRadm@gen.cam.ac.uk.

In your CV, please identify your three most significant papers and provide a brief statement about their contribution. We appreciate explanatory text to provide context and highlight the importance of selected outputs as in narrative CVs. As signatories of DORA (https://sfdora.org/) we do not use journal titles or Impact Factors to assess research quality and candidates should not include uncontextualised citation counts or other metrics such as h-index in their applications.

If you would like to informally discuss this opportunity, please contact our Head of Department, Professor Steve Russell sr120@cam.ac.uk.

Please quote reference PC44210 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

Post Doctoral Research Associate in Generative Protein Design and Microfluidic Assembly

Job id: 163965. Salary: £45,031 - £48,607 per annum inclusive of London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 26 November 2026. Closing date: 10 December 2026.

Business unit: Natural, Mathematical & Engineering Sci. Department: Chemistry.

Contact details: Mark Wallace. mark.wallace@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About Us

A new ARIA-funded programme is building programmable protein-templated materials across research groups at King's College London and the University of Bristol. The team brings together the Wallace Lab (membrane biophysics, microfluidics and single-molecule imaging, KCL Chemistry), the Photonics and Nanotechnology Research Group (plasmonics and nanomaterials fabrication, KCL Physics), and the Woolfson and Boyle labs (de novo protein design, Bristol).

King's College London is one of the UK's leading research universities, ranked in the top 40 globally. The Department of Chemistry was ranked 5th in the UK in the 2021 Research Excellence Framework, with 98% of research assessed as internationally excellent. The Department of Physics is home to internationally recognised expertise in plasmonics, metamaterials, and optical nanomaterials.

About The Role

The programme aims to build a new class of programmable 2D materials from designed proteins, with applications in molecular separation and nanophotonic metamaterials. The scientific challenge is to go from angstrom-level molecular precision to large-area functional materials. Our platform couples de novo protein design with multiphase microfluidics to direct the assembly of designed membrane and membrane-associated proteins at fluid interfaces, followed by mineralisation into robust inorganic frameworks.

The two posts will be led by Prof Mark Wallace and embedded at King's, joining a postdoctoral team already appointed at King's and Bristol. The candidates will adapt and develop our generative design pipeline to create membrane and membrane-associated proteins, including channel and pore-forming proteins, taking those designs through expression, purification and functional test. You will pair that design work with multiphase microfluidics to concentrate, orient and assemble designed proteins at lipidic interfaces, validated with single-molecule optical imaging.

Day to day you will run complete design-build-test cycles: generating candidate sequences; producing them recombinantly or cell-free; and with the support

of the wider team characterise the assembly and transport behaviour using single-molecule imaging, vesicle efflux and single-channel recording. These posts focus on integrating generative design approaches taken to the bench and/or in candidates who bring membrane protein production or interface microfluidics alongside it.

These are 2x full-time posts (35 hours per week) and will be offered a fixed term contract until 31/05/2028 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension until 31/08/2029 subject to the ARIA milestone review in February 2027.

About You

You will hold a PhD (or have submitted your thesis and be awaiting award) in biochemistry, biophysics, chemistry, physics, materials science, or a closely related discipline, with a track record of independent research demonstrated by scientific publication. You will have hands-on experience of generative or computational protein design and of producing proteins yourself at the bench, and you will be comfortable moving between a terminal and a wet lab. You will be collaborative, direct about what you know and don't know, and motivated by working on a hard scientific problem with a team built specifically around it.

This post requires both computational design and experimental protein work. Please address each essential criterion explicitly in your supporting statement, naming the design tools you have used, the designs you took forward to experimental test, and the proteins you have expressed and purified yourself.

Essential criteria

PhD (or thesis submitted and awaiting award) in a relevant discipline: biochemistry, biophysics, chemistry, physics, materials science, or closely related field. 
A track record of independent research demonstrated by first-author publications in peer-reviewed international journals.
Practical experience with generative or computational protein design tools, including designs taken forward to experimental test OR experience with lipid membrane systems or multiphase microfluidics: droplet interface bilayers, supported lipid bilayers, liposomes, droplet generation, or microfluidic device design and fabrication.
Hands-on experience with recombinant expression and purification of membrane or membrane-associated proteins, in E. coli and/or cell-free systems, including detergent solubilisation or membrane reconstitution. 
Ability to plan, execute, and troubleshoot experimental research independently and to a high standard. 
Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex data to interdisciplinary audiences. 
Ability to work collaboratively within a multi-site team and to contribute openly to shared goals. 

Desirable criteria

Experience with ion-channel or nanopore characterisation, including single-channel recording or vesicle efflux assays.
Experience with single-molecule fluorescence or label-free imaging, for example TIRF, interferometric scattering microscopy, or mass photometry.
Experience with automation or high-throughput screening in support of rapid design-build-test cycles.
Experience supervising or mentoring PhD students or junior researchers, or contributing to grant applications or intellectual property development.
Experience in a fast-paced, milestone-driven research environment, including funded programmes with funder reporting requirements. 

 Please note that this is a PhD-level role, but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhD will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5 with the title of Research Assistant, upgrading to Grade 6 Research Associate upon confirmation of the PhD award.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 11 January 2027

 

The Role

 

The purpose of this role is for a skilled MRI physicist to design and deliver high-quality clinical research in magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy within the Centre for In Vivo Imaging at Newcastle University. This is a role which will embrace working with a principal investigator and collaborating with an multi-disciplinary team of scientists and clinicians.

 

There are two 3.0T research-dedicated Philips MRI scanners, with pulse programming and advanced scan capabilities. Studies are supported by a dedicated research radiography team.

 

The research interests of the Centre for In Vivo Imaging (CIVI, https://www.ncl.ac.uk/civi) are wide-ranging, covering most of the research disciplines within in the Translational and Clinical Research Institute, and the wider Faculty of Medical Sciences. These include studies of function and metabolism in the brain and most organs of the body. The Centre has particular interests in multinuclear imaging/spectroscopy (19F, 23Na, 31P, 13C, 7Li). CIVI works alongside the many clinical academics within the Faculty of Medical Sciences, and clinician researchers in the local acute and mental health NHS Trusts, to design and deliver high impact translational research that improves health. The post-holder would develop and support such studies.

 

This post is available on a fixed term basis until 30th June 2029. The post could suit equally those who have just qualified with a PhD, or those with postdoctoral experience. Newcastle University is committed to career development for Research Associates through development to independent research and/or staff scientist positions where appropriate. Informal questions about the position can be addressed to Dr Kieren Hollingsworth (kieren.hollingsworth@newcastle.ac.uk).

 

 

Key Accountabilities

Working under the guidance of academic staff, develop and carry out research using appropriate magnetic resonance imaging/spectroscopy and equipment available within the Centre for In Vivo Imaging
Determine appropriate methodologies for research, showing an appropriate degree of independence, with advice and support where required
Review the literature to assess proposals for research by collaborating principal investigators to determine scientific right-to-succeed and appropriate resourcing
Writing up and publication of own/collaborative research through publications in leading peer-reviewed journals
Prepare high quality presentations and present research findings at national/international conferences/meetings and to appropriate stakeholders within the University
Work with the support staff and, with undergraduate and postgraduate students, and interact intellectually with other academic members of the Institute
May contribute to events celebrating the public engagement of translational research
Contribute to funding applications submitted by others
Contribute to the program of teaching within the Centre of In Vivo Imaging, including the MSc in Clinical Science (Medical Physics) and other courses as appropriate

 

 

The Person 

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

Experience in delivering research project(s)
Experience of developing, and validating acquisition methods in magnetic resonance imaging/spectroscopy
Experience of developing and devising analysis techniques for MRI/MRS data
Evidence of interpretation of data and investigations leading to the discovery of new knowledge
Evidence of independent working and initiative in research work, under the broad guidance of academic staff

Desirable

Publication record in PhD and postdoctoral work, reflecting a productive role within research teams (first author and/or middle author publications). The role the individual played in publications should be stated
Evidence of managing projects and/or interactions with principal investigators
Experience of providing successful advice to non-expert scientific users of MRI/MRS
Experience of teaching of magnetic resonance physics
Experience of delivering research that exploits academic knowledge in a commercial or applied setting
Knowledge of Philips pulse sequence programming
Experience of public engagement activities

 

 

Attributes and Behaviour

Ability to undertake research and analysis independently, with guidance from academic staff
Able to effectively organise allocated work activities
Excellent organisational, communication and interpersonal skills
Ability to carry out research project work within agreed timelines, meeting project milestones and producing research to an appropriate standard

 

 

Qualifications

PhD in magnetic resonance imaging and/or spectroscopy, preferably on in-vivo clinical or pre-clinical work

About the Role

 

This is a full-time (36.5 hrs/week) fixed-term contract ending no later than 3rd January 2030. Contract length will depend on the agreed salary due to restricted budget.

 

We are seeking to appoint a Research Fellow for the BBSRC Project ‘Development of a paired, preterm infant research simulator and digital twin to accelerate high-risk neonatal transport research’ led at Warwick by Prof. Declan Bates and Dr. Sina Saffaran.

 

The overall goal of the project is to develop new digital twins of pre-term neonates that can be used to conduct research into the safest transport strategies for these high-risk patients.

 

You will join our dynamic team who are conducting internationally leading research on the development and application of digital twins to critical care medicine.

 

You will undertake independent and collaborative research and will be expected to write up your research for publication.

 

You will be expected to deal with any management/administration problems that may arise from the project and produce and present regular project reports ensuring that the project objectives and deadlines are met. 

 

This post is based at the University of Warwick (in the ICSM Lab at the School of Engineering). However, the successful candidate will be required to make trips to the project partners, who are based in Nottingham and London.

 

This is an excellent opportunity for someone previously researching the application of digital twins to research in respiratory and critical care medicine.

 

About You

 

You will have a good honours degree (minimum 2:1) or equivalent in a relevant subject, alongside a PhD (or equivalent), or be nearing completion, in a relevant discipline such as Engineering, Materials Science or Physics.

 

You will have background knowledge of the application of digital twins to research in respiratory and critical care medicine, together with a developing research profile and the ability to produce high-quality research outputs and publications in this area.

 

You will have sufficient breadth and/or depth of specialist knowledge, including an understanding of relevant research methods and techniques, to contribute effectively to established research programmes.

You will also have the ability and potential to contribute to the development of funding proposals to secure external funding and support future research projects.

 

You will be an effective and collaborative team member, able to build positive working relationships with academic and professional services colleagues, both within and outside the University.

 

You will be committed to contributing to a supportive and collegial environment and to the wider life of the School, including supporting activities such as offer holder days and outreach events, which may occasionally require weekend working.

 

You will have good IT skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office, and the ability to use digital tools effectively to prepare technical research papers, reports and presentations.

 

The ability to code in Matlab will constitute a distinct advantage.

 

 

About the Department

 

The post will be based within the School of Engineering at the University of Warwick, which is one of the leading unified Engineering schools in the UK.

 

For further information regarding the skills required for this role please see the personal specification section of the attached job description.

 

The University aims to promote work life balance for all employees and the School of Engineering will consider a range of possible flexible working arrangements in order to recruit the best candidate.

 

The School of Engineering is a great place to work. We offer competitive salaries on a grading structure that provides annual incremental progression, plus a generous annual leave entitlement (30 days per annum for this role, plus four customary closure days over Christmas, and eight statutory bank holidays). As well as competitive salaries, we offer attractive pension schemes with excellent employer contributions, and various staff recognition awards. We are also committed to helping you to fulfil your potential through a range of career development opportunities.

 

The School of Engineering is committed to the principles of the Athena SWAN Charter, which recognises work undertaken to address gender equality, representation and progression for all staff working in an academic environment. The School currently holds the Athena SWAN Gold award and the University holds an Institutional Silver award. Further information about the work of the School in relation to Athena SWAN can be found at the following link; Athena SWAN - School of Engineering - University of Warwick

 

 

How to Apply

 

To apply, please click APPLY below and submit an application form by the closing deadline.

 

You will be asked to add your personal details and include two attachments:

 

CV
Cover Letter

 

These attachments should:

 

Outline employment and education history (including your most recent employment).
Demonstrate your skills, experience, and qualifications, and how you meet the essential and desirable criteria in the Job Description (attached below).

 

Please ensure your application clearly evidences the essential criteria, as the hiring panel may not be able to shortlist your application if these are not demonstrated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage candidates to submit an application as early as possible.

 

Interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed.

 

Job Description

 

For more information about essential and desirable knowledge, skills, experience, and qualifications for this position, please refer to the Job Description (JD) by clicking the link below:

 

↪ JD - Research Fellow (649)

 

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5.

 

Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow level, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6.

 

Benefits

 

At the University of Warwick, you will have access to a wide range of benefits.

 

an attractive pension scheme;
a leading annual leave allowance;
excellent learning and development opportunities;
savings and discounts on a wide range of products and services;
generous maternity, paternity, and adoption leave;
onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work-life balance and support flexible working where this is compatible with the requirements of the role. Click here to find out more.

 

We are proud to be a Living Wage Employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, our Relocation Guide provides information about working at the University of Warwick and what may be involved in the relocation process.

 

Culture

 

At the University of Warwick, committed to creating a community built on mutual respect and dignity, and a welcoming working and learning environment.

 

We recognise and value the visible and non-visible differences within our community. Wherever possible, we seek to go beyond our legal obligations by removing economic, social, and cultural barriers to creating an environment in which everyone has the opportunity to thrive and achieve their full potential.

 

We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and communities, regardless of age, disability, sex or gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion or belief, sexual or romantic orientation, culture or background. Job Title: Research Fellow (112569)

Reference:  630             

Department: Life Sciences

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 31 March 2030

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Thursday 17 December 2026, 11:59 pm                        

Full time Salary Range: £37,369 - £46,970 per annum

About the Role

Applications are invited for a post-doctoral scientist to join the Martins group in the School of Life Sciences, University of Warwick, working on a BBSRC-funded project (“Multi-Level Regulation of the Cyanobacterial Cell Division Cycle by the Circadian Oscillator”). The project’s aim is to investigate how circadian timing, cellular metabolism and cell-division processes interact in cyanobacteria to determine when cells divide. The project builds on previous work in the group and offers an opportunity to contribute to an interdisciplinary programme combining quantitative microbiology, live-cell imaging and systems biology.

 

The Martins Lab is based at the School of Life Sciences, Gibbet Hill Campus. We are an interdisciplinary research group studying how cells integrate information to coordinate growth, physiology and gene expression. The group combines quantitative experiments, microscopy, microfluidics, synthetic biology and mathematical modelling, and works closely with collaborators across the School of Life Sciences and beyond.

 

We and the wider University of Warwick environment offer substantial opportunities for professional development including regular opportunities to attend international conferences.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are looking for someone with expertise in microbiology, systems biology, cell biology, biochemistry, biophysics, bioengineering or a related discipline, with experience and demonstrated interest in fundamental quantitative biology and time-lapse fluorescence microscopy. Applicants should be proficient in or have a proven ability in relevant research and research methods and techniques, such as molecular biology and bacterial transformations, single-cell fluorescence microscopy and/or microfluidics, quantitative image analysis, microbial metabolism and energetics, and familiarity with quantitative biology approaches.

 

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£36,320 per annum).

 

Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£37,369 per annum).

About the Department

School of Life Sciences

 

For further information about the School of Life Sciences please see our website.

 

We believe that collegiality, openness, inclusivity and diversity are essential for an excellent research and teaching environment. Our workplace ethic has enabled us to gain the Athena SWAN Silver award. We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage applications from all groups with protected characteristics traditionally under-represented in STEM fields. As part of our ongoing commitment to addressing gender equality under the Athena Swan chartermark, we would particularly encourage and welcome applications from female academics.

 

Hybrid Working:

Due to the nature of this role, there is an expectation that the postholder will spend a minimum of 80% of their time working on campus. There may be periods requiring 100% on-campus presence in order to complete specific experiments, particularly within the first three months to support training. Following successful completion of the training period, hybrid working may be available, typically allowing for one day per week working from home.

How to Apply

Applications should include a CV and a covering letter expressing your most recent employment experience, your motivation. along with any additional relevant experience and education history; including the reasons for your interest in this post.  Within this information you should demonstrate how you meet the requirements of this role by specific reference to each of the essential and desirable critera, and where applicable, detailed in the person specification.

 

This information will be used in the shortlisting process and without this evidence we may not be able to shortlist your application.

 

Please note that if you do not evidence the essential requirements, we may not be able to shortlist your application.

 

In your application, you can also include any career breaks you may have taken (e.g. parental/caring/long-term sick leave, part-time work, secondments) or any periods where you were unable or restricted to work because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated.

The interviews will be held on TBC

Any requests for further information about the role can be directed to Bruno Martins, bruno.martins@warwick.ac.uk 

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.
